chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd narrated from his brother Jaʿfar ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, from ʿAlī ibn Yaqṭīn, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who appointed a woman as his executor and joined with her in the bequest a young boy. He said: “That is permissible. The woman carries out the bequest and does not wait for the boy to reach maturity. Then when the boy reaches maturity, he has no right to withhold approval except in the case of alteration or change; then he has the right to return it to what the deceased had bequeathed.”

key_terms.أَوْصَى: appointed through a bequest or testamentary instruction
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the deceased person who made the will
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: the bequest or will to be carried out after death
key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman appointed in the role of executor
key_terms.تَبْدِيلٍ: alteration or substitution in the terms of the will
key_terms.تَغْيِيرٍ: change made to the original bequest
key_terms.صَبِيًّا: a minor boy not yet legally mature

ai.seo_question: Can a woman carry out a will if a minor is appointed with her as co-executor?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a bequest in which a woman and a minor are jointly appointed. It establishes that the woman may execute the will immediately, while the minor, upon maturity, may only intervene if the will has been altered from the deceased's original instruction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5486 - Muhammad bin Isa bin Ubaid narrated from his brother Ja'far bin Isa bin Ubaid, from Ali bin Yaqtin, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (as) about a man who appointed a woman as his executor and included a child with her in the will.
Imam (as) said: "This is permissible. The woman should carry out the will and does not need to wait for the child to reach maturity. However, when the child grows up, he has no right to object unless there has been an alteration or change in the will, in which case he has the right to restore it to what the deceased had originally intended."
